title: Function st.sandbox() to embed AI generated Streamlit Code
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I would like to propose a new st.sandbox() function that can be used to execute AI-generated Streamlit code for visualization purposes without introducing security risks. This could give users the possibility to create their own dashboards using a chat function.

### Why?

I tried to add different visualizations in a Chatbot within Streamlit. As my Chatbot gives the user the opportunity to chat with our database, I would like to visualize the result received from my agent. I added some functions that offer different visualizations like plotly diagrams and maps, but this procedure is static and not flexible.
I also tried to create html code and embed it with st.html(), but the result was not consistent with the theming and looked awful. I checked also other existing python packages for this purpose but I had the impression they are not reliable. Maybe the limitation on streamlit functions (and limited additional packages) might be easier also from security perspective.

### How?

Something like the following code would maybe be nice:

```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "month": ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"],
    "sales": [120, 150, 180]
    })

llm_code = """
import plotly.express as px
fig = px.bar(df, x="month", y="sales")
st.plotly_chart(fig)
"""

result = st.sandbox(
    dataframe=df,
    code=llm_code,
    allowed_packages=[
        "streamlit",
        "pandas",
        "plotly"
    ])

if result.status == "success":
    st.success("Code executed successfully")

elif result.status == "error":
    st.warning(result.error_message)

elif result.status == "security_violation":
    st.error(result.error_message)
```
